title: Why Do Turkey Fryers Explode? Thanksgiving Is the Peak Day for US Home Cooking Fires
fb_caption: Thanksgiving is the peak day of the year for home cooking fires in the US, according to the National Fire Protection Association, and the NFPA discourages turkey fryers that use cooking oil. So why do they go wrong so fast? Three big reasons: too much oil that spills onto the burner, ice and water that flash into steam, and oil that keeps heating with no temperature control. If you do fry: thaw the bird completely, test the oil level with water first, fry outside on level ground, and never leave it alone. Has anyone in your family ever deep-fried a turkey? Tell us below.

beats.text: Thanksgiving is the peak day of the year for home cooking fires in America. That's from the National Fire Protection Association. And it discourages one cooking method: the oil turkey fryer.

items: PEAK DAY FOR HOME COOKING FIRES

beats.text: So why do turkey fryers go wrong so fast? Here are the three big reasons.

One: too much oil. A turkey is big. Lower it into a full pot and the oil level rises. It can spill over the rim, straight down onto the open burner underneath. Even a small spill can turn into a large fire.

items: A SMALL SPILL, A LARGE FIRE

beats.text: Two: ice and water. A turkey that is still partly frozen is carrying water. When water hits hot oil, it flashes into steam. Steam takes up far more room, so it shoves the oil up and out of the pot.
Three: runaway heat. Some fryers have no temperature control. Leave the burner on and the oil keeps getting hotter, until it can catch fire.
Think of a bathtub filled to the brim. Step in, and the water has to go somewhere. Now picture that water as hot oil, with a flame under the tub.

items: THE WATER HAS TO GO SOMEWHERE

beats.text: Where you fry matters too. Fire departments warn against using a fryer in a garage or on a wooden deck, where spilled oil can spread a fire to the house.
Takeaway: thaw the bird completely and pat it dry. Test the oil level with water first. Fry outside, on level ground, away from anything that burns. Never leave it alone. Or choose an oil-free fryer.

items: THAW IT COMPLETELY, PAT IT DRY
TEST THE OIL LEVEL WITH WATER

beats.text: Has anyone in your family ever deep-fried a turkey? Tell us how it went in the comments, and send this to whoever is cooking this year. Because Thanksgiving is the peak day for home cooking fires.
